answer: Bonded identities with slashable deposits: an agent must lock real stake before it can transact, and any peer who proves fraud gets the bond slashed to them. Sybils can wander through an ocean of fake accounts, but each one costs upfront capital like fueling a comet on every launch, so the swarm's cost grows linearly while a single honest identity stays cheap. Identities that move in lockstep forfeit as a cluster, making mass forgery unprofitable.
